ar-71f95389.stem: Which of the following joints is a syndesmosis?
options: Attachment of the teeth to their sockets
ar-71f95389.explanation: A syndesmosis is a fibrous joint in which bones are joined by a ligament or membrane: the distal tibiofibular joint and the interosseous membranes of the forearm and leg are examples. The pubic symphysis is fibrocartilaginous, the 1st sternocostal joint a synchondrosis, the tooth–socket union a gomphosis, and sutures are fibrous joints peculiar to the skull.

ar-296e0313.stem: Which of the following is a saddle (sellar) synovial joint?
ar-296e0313.explanation: In saddle joints both surfaces are concave in one direction and convex in the other; they allow movement about two axes, including opposition. Examples: the 1st carpometacarpal joint and the sternoclavicular joint. The radiocarpal joint is ellipsoid, the humero-ulnar a hinge, the proximal radio-ulnar a pivot and the acromioclavicular a plane joint.

ar-ca13fe9c.stem: Which of the following pairings is WRONG?
ar-ca13fe9c.explanation: The atlanto-occipital joint is ellipsoid (condylar) and allows the 'yes' movement. Pivot joints are the median atlanto-axial joint ('no' movement) and the proximal and distal radio-ulnar joints.

ar-244f637a.stem: The growth plate (epiphyseal plate) is an example of which type of joint?
ar-244f637a.explanation: In primary cartilaginous joints (synchondroses) bones are joined by hyaline cartilage and most ossify with time: the epiphyseal plate, the 1st rib–manubrium joint, the spheno-occipital synchondrosis. Secondary cartilaginous joints (symphyses) contain fibrocartilage and lie in the midline.

ar-230a765a.stem: Which of the following about the temporomandibular joint is FALSE?
options: Part of the lateral pterygoid attaches to the disc.
On opening the mouth, the condyle and disc glide forwards towards the articular tubercle.
The articular disc divides the joint into upper and lower cavities.
The articular surfaces are covered with hyaline cartilage.
Hinge (rotation) movement occurs in the lower joint cavity.
ar-230a765a.explanation: The articular surfaces of the TMJ are covered with fibrocartilage, not hyaline cartilage (related to the intramembranous origin of the bones). The disc divides the joint in two: rotation occurs in the lower cavity, forward gliding (translation) in the upper. Lateral pterygoid pulls the condyle and disc forwards.

ar-30f33bcd.stem: A patient who yawned cannot close the mouth. The mandibular condyle has passed in front of the articular tubercle. In which direction is the jaw pushed for reduction?
ar-30f33bcd.explanation: TMJ dislocation is almost always anterior; the condyle catches in front of the eminence and spasm of the muscles (masseter, temporalis, medial pterygoid) holds it there. With the thumbs on the lower molars the jaw is pushed first downwards (to pass beneath the eminence) and then backwards.

ar-56a27913.stem: The gelatinous centre of the intervertebral disc (nucleus pulposus) is embryologically a remnant of what?
ar-56a27913.explanation: The nucleus pulposus is a remnant of the notochord; the surrounding anulus fibrosus consists of fibrocartilaginous rings of sclerotomal origin. With age its water content falls and disc height decreases.

ar-b272030c.stem: Why are lumbar disc herniations most often posterolateral?
options: The anterior longitudinal ligament supports the back.
The anulus fibrosus is thicker posteriorly.
The posterior longitudinal ligament is thick in the midline and thin at the sides.
The nucleus pulposus lies near the front of the disc.
The ligamentum flavum pushes the disc from the sides.
ar-b272030c.explanation: The posterior longitudinal ligament is a narrow band behind the vertebral bodies and supports the disc only in the midline. The anulus fibrosus is also thinner posteriorly. So the nucleus pulposus herniates most often posterolaterally and compresses the nerve root.

ar-a0beeda5.stem: Which yellow ligament, rich in elastic fibres, runs between the laminae of the vertebral arches?
ar-a0beeda5.explanation: The ligamenta flava join adjacent laminae; thanks to their elastic fibres they help straighten the spine after flexion. In lumbar puncture the needle passes the skin, supraspinous and interspinous ligaments and then the ligamentum flavum (a 'pop') to reach the epidural space.

ar-0918e232.stem: At which joint does most of the 'no' movement (rotation) of the head occur?
ar-0918e232.explanation: At the atlanto-axial joints (one median pivot and two lateral plane joints) the atlas rotates around the dens; about half of neck rotation occurs here. The 'yes' movement is at the atlanto-occipital joint. The alar ligaments limit excessive rotation.

ar-24e0cc41.stem: Which joint does the head of a rib form with the bodies of two adjacent thoracic vertebrae?
options: Joint of the head of the rib
ar-24e0cc41.explanation: The head of a typical rib forms the joint of the head of the rib with the demifacets on the bodies of two adjacent vertebrae and the intervening disc; its tubercle forms the costotransverse joint with the transverse process of the lower vertebra. These two joints allow the rib's 'bucket-handle' and 'pump-handle' movements in breathing.

ar-e90c051e.stem: Which is the only true (synovial) joint connecting the upper limb to the axial skeleton?
ar-e90c051e.explanation: The only articular connection between the upper limb and the axial skeleton is the sternoclavicular joint. It is a saddle joint with an articular disc and very strong support from the costoclavicular ligament; so it rarely dislocates, and clavicle fracture is more common. The scapulothoracic 'joint' is not a true joint.

ar-55314209.stem: A rugby player who fell on his shoulder has a step between the acromion and clavicle, with the outer end of the clavicle prominent above. Which ligament must also be torn for this (type III) separation?
ar-55314209.explanation: In acromioclavicular separation, if only the AC ligament tears the step is slight. If the coracoclavicular ligament (conoid and trapezoid parts) also tears, the scapula and arm drop and the end of the clavicle stays markedly high.

ar-94215574.stem: A volleyball player falls with the arm abducted and externally rotated. A shoulder dislocation is found, and after reduction there is sensory loss over the outer shoulder. What is the direction of the dislocation and which nerve is injured?
ar-94215574.explanation: The glenohumeral joint is the most frequently dislocated large joint in the body; more than 95% of dislocations are anteroinferior because the lower part of the capsule is weakest. As the humeral head descends, the axillary nerve just below the surgical neck is stretched.
